IEEPA refunds · Verified 2026-11-14

IEEPA duty refunds: CAPE or the CIT

In short

  • By default, CBP pays a refund to the importer of record (19 CFR 24.36(b)).
  • CAPE: CBP's refund declaration in ACE. Only the importer of record, or the broker that filed the entry, can submit it (CSMS #68340863).
  • CAPE declaration on a liquidated entry · Within 80 days after liquidation, counted to the date the CAPE declaration is filed (CBP acceptance rule)
  • protest · 180 days after liquidation or reliquidation · 19 U.S.C. 1514(c)(3)
  • This page computes no date for your entries. Whether any window is open depends on each entry's liquidation date, which only your ACE report shows.

Key dates

Date Event Source
2026-02-20 Supreme Court: IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, No. 24-1287) Opinion
2026-02-24 CBP stopped collecting IEEPA duties on goods entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption from 12:00 a.m. ET CSMS #67834313
2026-04-20 CAPE opened (Phase 1) CSMS #68315804, CSMS #68340863
2026-10-08 The CIT certified a class (Freestyle World, Inc. v. CBP, No. 26-01088) Slip Op. 26-123

Who receives the refund

By default, CBP pays a refund to the importer of record (19 CFR 24.36(b)). The importer of record can use CBP Form 4811 to have it paid to another party (19 CFR 24.36(a)). Other rules apply where an owner's declaration was filed or a surety paid.

If your courier, customs broker or U.S. buyer was the importer of record, CBP pays that party unless one of these rules applies. Whether you can recover from that party is a separate question.

Two routes

CAPE

CAPE: CBP's refund declaration in ACE. Only the importer of record, or the broker that filed the entry, can submit it (CSMS #68340863). Bandi & Associates PLLC does not file CAPE declarations.

CAPE phases

2026-04-20: CAPE opened for certain entries not yet liquidated and certain entries within 80 days of liquidation (CSMS #68315804).

2026-06-29: CAPE began taking certain entries flagged for reconciliation (CSMS #69066837).

In a 2026-09-15 court declaration, CBP said Phase 3 would deploy on 2026-10-06 for finally liquidated entries of CIT plaintiffs where the court ordered reliquidation; Phase 3 is open only to CIT plaintiffs (Lord Decl. ¶8).

A protest, then the CIT

For entries CAPE does not take. A protest is filed with CBP (19 U.S.C. 1514) and, where needed, an action is brought at the CIT. Whether the class the CIT certified on 2026-10-08 covers an entry is assessed entry by entry.

Who may file a protest; the class

The importer of record or consignee, or an authorized agent such as a customs broker or an attorney, may file a protest (19 CFR 174.12(a), 174.3).

The class in Freestyle World, Inc. v. CBP (No. 26-01088, Slip Op. 26-123, certified 2026-10-08): each importer of record that paid IEEPA duties between 2025-02-01 and 2026-02-19, except any that filed its own action to recover IEEPA duties. The order directs no refund. The government's appeal of the CIT's reliquidation order was docketed at the Federal Circuit on 2026-06-03 (No. 26-1895).

What decides the route
  1. Whether each entry is not yet liquidated, was liquidated within the last 80 days, or was liquidated earlier (CSMS #68340863).
  2. Whether a protest was filed within 180 days after liquidation (19 U.S.C. 1514(c)(3)).
  3. Who was the importer of record, and whether it has ACE access or a filing broker (CSMS #68315804).
  4. Whether the entry type is one CAPE accepts in its current phase (CSMS #68340863, #69066837).
  5. Whether you are already a plaintiff at the CIT, or a member of the class the CIT certified.

Periods that may apply

Clock Potential window Basis On this page
CAPE declaration on a liquidated entry Within 80 days after liquidation, counted to the date the CAPE declaration is filed (CBP acceptance rule) CBP CSMS #68340863 (2026-04-13), #69066837 (2026-06-29); CBP cites no statute for this period POTENTIAL · liquidation date UNKNOWN
protest 180 days after liquidation or reliquidation 19 U.S.C. 1514(c)(3) POTENTIAL · liquidation date UNKNOWN
CIT action after a denied protest 180 days after notice of the denial is mailed, or 180 days after a denial by operation of law 28 U.S.C. 2636(a)(1)–(2) POTENTIAL
CIT action under 28 U.S.C. 1581(i) 2 years after the cause of action first accrues 28 U.S.C. 2636(i) UNKNOWN · accrual date not determined by any rule this page cites

This page computes no date for your entries. Whether any window is open depends on each entry's liquidation date, which only your ACE report shows.

If a CAPE window on any of your entries may close soon, do not wait for this report: the importer of record, or the broker that filed the entry, can declare it in CAPE now. Nothing in this engagement stops or extends any period.

What to gather
  • Your ACE entry report, with entry numbers, entry dates, liquidation dates or status, IEEPA duties deposited and the date each was paid.
  • Your broker's CAPE acceptance reports and refund records, or "none".
  • Whether you were the importer of record on those entries, and whether an owner's declaration was filed.
  • Whether you have filed any protest or court action.

Do not send any of this yet. The conflict check comes first and needs names only.

The foreign IOR rule

From 2027-01-05 a foreign IOR needs CTPAT validation or a CTPAT-validated licensed customs broker (19 CFR 141.21(b), FR 2026-22735). See the rule.
